mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 700K units, indicating strengthening demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 700K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as investors seek higher yields.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) drops below 6% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200K in a month, the combined labor market strength predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a quarter, indicating supply chain disruptions, leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate decreased earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 55% of instances when INDPRO declines > 2%, or Rank IC < 0.025 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Real GDP (GDPC1) growth above 3% in a quarter, signaling robust demand, predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate sustained economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 45% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 3%, or Rank IC < 0.015 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 50 basis points in a month, indicating monetary tightening, leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors adjust to higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS increases > 50bps, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth is above 1.5% in a quarter, the strong labor market predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, but only during non-recessionary periods.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS growth > 1.5% in 1 quarter
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market and recession data
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of non-recessionary instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Retail and food services sales (RSAFS) growth above 5% in a month, indicating strong consumer spending, predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as investors anticipate sustained demand-driven growth.
evidence_refs: fact:historical retail sales and market correlations
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when RSAFS growth > 5%, or Rank IC < 0.012 over any 3-year rolling window.
